control.name: CONTROL — remove the append-only shrink guard entirely (a whole-file PUT that reverts rows ships as success)

mutations.name: the --root join becomes a no-op (a repo-relative --evidence-file is read from the process cwd, not the --root checkout — #1709 defeated)
drop the absolute-path-with---root refusal (an absolute --evidence-file silently ignores --root instead of being refused)
disarm the shrink comparison (a commit with FEWER rows than the remote is no longer refused — unattributable row deletion ships)
scan the whole merged file instead of the bytes this landing adds (a brief already carrying a secret-shaped run can never receive an Evidence append again — #901/#966/#1161 re-opened)
addedLines stops subtracting the lines the branch already carries (every line of the commit is scanned as new — a Verify row's own quoted run re-refuses forever, #1161)
drop the origin from a scan refusal (the operator is back to isolating by hand which line tripped it — #1161 ask 3)
drop the pre-existing notice (a brief carrying a secret-shaped run lands silently; nothing tells the operator the scan saw it and where — #1161 ask 3)
drop the row-scope rebase (a stale local README landing reverts every foreign row again — the whole class this guard exists to close)
unwire the row-scope write-op second layer at its only call site (a table change between the pre-check and the write is overwritten — the layer behind the single point of failure is gone)
drop the write's ExpectedSHA precondition (a table change after the write-time re-check is overwritten by the backend's own fetch-and-PUT — the race is narrowed, not closed)
drop the fail-closed malformed-marker refusal (a README whose marker drifted or shares a line lands as an unguarded whole-file write)
drop the named-row-absent-from-remote refusal (contract item 4 — the missing key indexes line 0)
drop the named-row-absent-from-local refusal (contract item 4 — local line 0 is spliced into the row)
drop the commit-only foreign-key arm of the write-time diagnostic (a refusal no longer names the row the commit added)
drop the remote duplicate-key refusal (last-wins keying clobbers a different brief's row)
drop the local duplicate-key refusal (which local line lands becomes a guess)
drop the named local row cell-count refusal (a truncated row lands and loses its lifecycle cells on the next regen)
drop the mid-line carriage-return refusal (a named line renders as an extra row)

drop the write-time whole-content comparison (the second layer accepts any drift the fresh fetch shows)
